title: finding(ci): nothing protects the `board-archive` orphan branch — and a delete does NOT cost one cycle, it discards the whole history the archive exists to keep
body:
## Summary

objectui#9387 adopts the board archiver so that **a GitHub account suspension cannot take the issue board with it** — the maintainer's stated purpose, since repositories survive a suspension and issues do not. The archive lands on an orphan branch, `board-archive`, written by `github-actions[bot]` four times a day.

⚠️ **Nothing configures how that branch is protected.** A delete or a force-push silently discards the archive — the one outcome the card exists to prevent.

## ⛔ The reasoning that makes this NOT self-healing

The tempting answer is 「the next run recreates it, so a delete costs one cycle」. That is **wrong on the facts**: the workflow recreates the **BRANCH**, not its **HISTORY**. A new orphan starts from an empty tree and the next run writes only the **current** board — so every earlier snapshot is gone, permanently, and the next run's green tick says nothing is wrong.

⇒ the failure is silent, total, and indistinguishable from health at exactly the moment the archive is supposed to be the thing that survived.

## What is needed

A ruleset on `board-archive` blocking **deletion** and **force-push**, leaving `github-actions[bot]`'s normal pushes intact.

⛔ **This is a maintainer action and cannot be a pull request**: repository settings are outside anything a PR can reach. Recorded here so it is not left to whoever notices the archive is missing.

## ⛔ What this card does NOT claim

- ⛔ NOT measured: whether any ruleset already covers `board-archive` by pattern. The branch does not exist yet (`git ls-remote --heads origin board-archive` = **0 refs**), so there is nothing to read; check before acting.
- ⛔ Not a blocker for objectui#9387 or PR objectui#10203. The archive is strictly better than no archive, and an unprotected one still survives the case the card is about.
- The R2 mirror is a second copy and a real answer to part of this, but it is ⛔ not configured — the four secrets are a separate maintainer action the adoption card explicitly leaves open.

Surfaced by the objectui#9387 dev as an out-of-scope finding; the history-vs-branch reasoning above is the part worth keeping and is why 「it regenerates」 is not a defence.

Dedupe words: `board-archive` · `orphan branch` · `force-push` · `ruleset` · `archive history lost`
